(UL1479), ASTM E1966 (UL2079) and CAN/ULC-S115 as well as to the time-temperature 
requirements of ASTM E119 (UL263). LCI provides up to a 4-hour fire rating for typical 
service penetrations through concrete or wood floors, concrete or masonry walls, as well as 
gypsum board walls. SpecSeal® LCI Sealant meets Class A finish requirements for Flame 
Spread and Smoke Development when tested in accordance with ASTM E84 (UL723). 
Meets or exceeds the requirements of ASTM C834, Type C, Grade 0. SpecSeal® LCI Sealant 
is also acoustically tested, demonstrating excellent sound attenuation properties.

excellent caulking properties as well as high build properties on vertical or overhead 
surfaces. This single component sealant may be caulked (standard cartridge or 
bulk loaded), knifed or troweled. In addition, SpecSeal® LCI Sealant does not contain 
PCB’s or asbestos.
SpecSeal® LCI Sealant is storage stable (when stored according to the 
manufacturer’s recommendations), and will not separate or shrink when dried 
(when applied according to the manufacturer's recommendations). SpecSeal® 
LCI Sealant will adhere to all common construction and penetrant materials and 
contains no solvents that might adversely effect plastic pipes or cable jackets.

messages.instruction_excerpt: Write the result of a submittal review for a busy project engineer. Plain language, no jargon, no model names. Give a one or two sentence summary, a short note to send to the subcontractor, a plain title for each issue, and one sentence on why each issue matters on site. Where an issue has a suggested_fix, name it in the note. Respect each coded verdict: unverified or not stated means missing evidence, not a failed requirement. Different revision labels alone do not establish which document is newer. Do not infer safety or code violations from a documentation difference.

messages.instruction_excerpt: Extract the product's stated properties from this submittal. Use these property names and meanings where they apply: {"cri": "Color quality (CRI)", "dim_min_percent": "Dims down to", "dlc_listed": "DLC listing", "document_revision": "Data sheet version", "efficacy_lm_per_w": "Efficiency (lumens per watt)", "f_rating_hr": "Fire rating (F)", "input_watts_120v": "Power at 120 V", "input_watts_277v": "Power at 277 V", "l70_hours": "Rated life (L70)", "lumens": "Light output", "macadam_steps": "macadam steps", "max_annular_space_in": "Largest gap it can seal", "penetrant_types": "Pipe types covered", "service_temp_max_f": "Highest service temperature", "service_temp_range_f": "Service temperature range", "standards": "Test standards", "t_rating_hr": "Temperature rating (T)", "voc_g_per_l": "VOC (air quality)", "warranty_years": "Warranty", "watts": "Power draw"}. Read every supplied page, including tables and notes. For a listed system, record its system number as model. Keep each test/rating metric distinct; never relabel a different metric to fit a requested name. Do not dump option tables. Omit SKU-dependent table values unless an exact submitted SKU is identified. A blank catalog-number field or an ordering example is not a submitted SKU selection. For other stated alternatives, retain distinct values without repeating the same value for every option. Record the page and a short supporting quote for each claim, and the revision or date printed on the data sheet. Copy each quote verbatim as one contiguous substring from that page; never paraphrase or join separate passages. Omit properties that are not stated instead of returning null claims. For lists, put each distinct standard or certification identifier in its own array entry. For covered pipe types, quote the enumerated penetrating-item list, not the wall studs or sleeves.
